name: Sleep your way to better mental health and wellbeing

content.title: Sleep your way to better mental health and wellbeing
content.summary: The role of quality sleep for optimal brain function and overall health

media.alt: Sleep your way to better mental health and wellbeing

content.text: Have there been days in your life when you have experienced fuzzy thinking, forgetfulness, increased anxiety, irritability and mood changes, and seemed to be causing accidents or getting injuries in ways you would ordinarily avoid? Does your appetite and weight seem untamed, struggling to concentrate on a task and you are getting more than your fair share of colds? Your body is trying to tell you something important, you need to rest better to allow your body to function better every day. How will your body achieve this? Through adequate sleep. But I do sleep, you wonder, but is it enough? Do you consistently get good quality and regular sleep?

It is often said that we sleep for a third of our lives. It seems quite a staggering amount of time for something we often take lightly in this day and age when everyone and everything around us is competing for our attention. From our family, school, work, colleagues, community and politicians to all manner of indoor, outdoor and online advertising to the constant buzz of activities on our smartphones. How much time is left for sleep?  Postponing sleep may seem like an ideal thing to do to free up time for other tasks but there are severe risks of skipping out on sleep.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), inadequate rest impairs the ability to think, handle stress, maintain a healthy immune system, and moderate emotions. Maintained total sleep deprivation is fatal in some animal species. The day after a night of abnormal or poor sleep is, whatever the cause, a disturbed day. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that adults should get at least 7 to 9 hours of sleep every night. Adults who sleep less than 7 hours a night may have more health issues than those who sleep 7 or more hours a night.
What is sleep?

Sleep is a necessary and reversible state of reduced activity that happens when we rest. It helps us feel better physically and mentally by helping us remember things better, control our emotions and heal our bodies.
What are the benefits of sleep?
Getting enough sleep has many benefits including:
1.Brain wellness: You feel better, remember and think more clearly and make good decisions easily when you get enough sleep.
2.Getting stuff done: Sleep helps you concentrate and be more productive.
3.Safer Driving: Enough sleep improves alertness, reaction time, and decision-making which are essential for safe driving.
4.Handle things better: Sleep lowers stress levels so you go about your day in a clear, well-thought-out way.
5.Remember more: You process, store new information and recall things better after a good night's sleep.
6.Stay healthy: Sleep helps your immune system fight off illness and stay strong.
7.Grow strong muscles: Sleep helps your body repair and restore the body, which can speed up muscle growth after exercise.
How do I improve my sleep?

By now, you must be wondering if there is something you can do to improve your sleeping habits. The good news is there are strategies to enhance the quality of your sleep. Let us take an in-depth look at three strategies used to improve sleep quality. They include:

1.Sleep Hygiene: This refers to both your sleep environment and behaviors. Consistency in sleep schedule, winding down before bed, creating a comfortable sleeping environment, avoiding electronics before bedtime, monitoring food and drink intake, and regular exercise are key components.

2.Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBTi): CBTi is a comprehensive treatment that addresses thoughts and behaviors related to sleep. It involves cognitive restructuring to correct unhelpful thoughts about sleep, changing behaviors through techniques like relaxation training and stimulus control, and providing educational support to understand the connection between thoughts, feelings, actions, and sleep.

Overall, it's essential to experiment with these strategies over time and seek guidance from a doctor, therapist, or sleep expert to determine the best treatment approach for individual needs. For easy reference to these simple steps towards sleeping better, download our Sleep Guide eBook here.
